name: Ard
title: Descendant of Benjamin and ancestor of the Ard clan
summary: Ard was a descendant of Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son, and the ancestor of the Ard clan within the tribe of Benjamin. He is mentioned in two different genealogies: In Genesis 46:21 he is counted among Benjamin's sons who went with Jacob to Egypt, while Numbers 26:40 specifies that he was a son of Bela, Benjamin's firstborn. Such differences in genealogical detail are common in biblical family trees, where the Hebrew word for 'son' (ben) includes both direct sons and more distant descendants. Ard's significance lies primarily in his role as founder of the Ard clan (ha-ardi), which was recorded in the census on the plains of Moab before the entry into Canaan. He may possibly be identified with Addar in 1 Chronicles 8:3, based on consonant interchange in the name.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jacob's family that went to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Ard is listed among the descendants of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob and his family. In the genealogy in Genesis, he is listed as one of Benjamin's sons, but this can be understood as a shorthand where grandsons are included under the grandfather's name.

keyEvents.title: Ancestor of the Ard clan in the census
keyEvents.description: In the census on the plains of Moab, Ard is mentioned as the son of Bela, son of Benjamin, and founder of the Ard clan (ha-ardi). Here the family relationship is specified more accurately than in Genesis, and the clan was registered with a view to land distribution in Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Possible identification with Addar in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles 8:3, 'Addar' is mentioned among Bela's sons. Several scholars believe this is a name variant of Ard based on consonant swapping (metathesis), which would then confirm his place in Bela's lineage.

versions.summary: Ard was a descendant of Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and Numbers as one of Benjamin's sons or grandsons. Through his descendants, the Ard clans within the tribe of Benjamin were established.
versions.title: Descendant of Benjamin
versions.reason: [minor] The title 'Descendant of Benjamin' is acceptable but could be refined. In Genesis 46:21, Ard is listed as a son of Benjamin, whereas Numbers 26:40 identifies him as a son of Bela (a son of Benjamin). A more precise title might be 'Descendant of Benjamin, ancestor of the Ard clan'.; [minor] The role 'patriarch' is somewhat exaggerated for Ard, who is primarily known as a clan leader or ancestor of a clan within the tribe of Benjamin. 'Clan leader' or 'ancestor' would be more accurate.; [minor] The summary is acceptable but should clarify the apparent contradiction between Genesis 46:21 (where Ard is listed as a son of Benjamin) and Numbers 26:40 (where Ard is a son of Bela, a son of Benjamin). This is a well-known textual critical issue.; [major] In 1 Chronicles 8:1–3, Ard is not explicitly mentioned. The verses list Bela, Ashbel, Ahrah, Noha, and Rafa (which varies between translations). Some identify 'Addar' in 1 Chronicles 8:3 as a possible variant of Ard, but this is uncertain. The reference should either be removed or made conditional with an explanatory footnote.; [minor] The last key event (Genesis 46:26–27) overlaps with the first (Genesis 46:21) and provides little new information specifically about Ard. It could have been merged or omitted to avoid redundancy.; [minor] 'c. 1800 BC' is a reasonable estimate for the patriarchal period, but the dating is uncertain and depends on the chronological framework. It may be more accurate to say 'c. 1800–1700 BC' or 'unknown, patriarchal period'.; [major] Footnotes are missing. Notes should be added regarding the textual critical issue between Genesis 46:21 and Numbers 26:40, and about the possible identification with Addar in 1 Chronicles 8:3.

versions.summary: Ard was a descendant of Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son. In Genesis 46:21 he is listed among Benjamin's sons who went to Egypt, while Numbers 26:40 identifies him as the son of Bela, Benjamin's firstborn. This difference is likely due to the Hebrew word for 'son' (ben) also meaning 'descendant.' Through Ard, the Ard clan (ha-ardi) was established within the tribe of Benjamin, a clan recorded during the census on the plains of Moab.
versions.title: Descendant of Benjamin and ancestor of the Ard clan
versions.reason: [minor] In Genesis 46:21 Ard is listed as a son of Benjamin, while Numbers 26:40 identifies him as a son of Bela. The profile has chosen Bela as the father, which is defensible based on the more detailed genealogy in Numbers, but it could have been useful to note that Genesis 46:21 names Benjamin directly. The current solution is acceptable.; [minor] The dating 'c. 1800–1700 BC' is very uncertain and difficult to establish for a figure known primarily from genealogies. Many chronologies place the patriarchal period and Jacob's journey to Egypt somewhat later (c. 1700–1600 BC). It may be worth considering using a broader formulation to reflect this uncertainty.; [minor] The summary is good and informative, but the sentence stating that the Hebrew word 'ben' can also mean 'descendant' is repeated almost verbatim in the footnotes. This is not an error, but there is some redundancy.

footnotes.text: In Gen 46:21 Ard is listed as a son of Benjamin, while Num 26:40 identifies him as a son of Bela, who in turn was a son of Benjamin. This apparent contradiction can be explained by the fact that 'son' in Hebrew (ben) can mean both son and descendant/grandson. Such generational simplifications are common in biblical genealogies.

The name Ard (Hebrew: אַרְדְּ) may mean 'fleeting' or 'one who goes down.' Some scholars have suggested a connection with the Hebrew verb yarad (ירד), meaning 'to go down,' which could be a symbolic name linked to the journey down to Egypt.

In 1 Chr 8:3 the name 'Addar' (אַדָּר) is mentioned among Bela's sons. Several biblical scholars believe this is a variant of 'Ard' (אַרְדְּ) where the consonants have been swapped (metathesis). If this identification is correct, it confirms that Ard was a son of Bela.

The Ard clan (ha-ardi) mentioned in Num 26:40 was one of the clans within the tribe of Benjamin counted during the census on the plains of Moab. Such clan divisions were important for land distribution in Canaan and military organization.

The tribe of Benjamin was one of the smallest tribes in Israel but held great strategic significance. The tribal territory lay between Judah and Ephraim and included Jerusalem. Ard's clan was one of the subgroups that contributed to the tribe's identity and organization.

The genealogies in Gen 46 have a summary character and list all of Jacob's household who went to Egypt, totaling 70 people. The number 70 had symbolic meaning in the ancient Near East and represented completeness and wholeness, which may have influenced how the lineages were structured in the text.
